reading.body:
Google operates a data center campus in Arcola, Loudoun County, Virginia as part of a multi-site footprint spanning Loudoun and Prince William counties. Google does not publish megawatt capacity, square footage, or specific building addresses for individual facilities, disclosing only aggregate state-level investment figures. The company announced a $1 billion expansion of these Northern Virginia campuses in April 2024, adding to existing sites designated Data Center 1 and Data Center 2.

This facility cannot be ranked by published power capacity because Google has not disclosed it. Among 326 mapped data center facilities in Virginia, only 23 have published megawatt figures in this registry, totaling 1,375 MW across the state. Google's Northern Virginia presence is material to the state's AI infrastructure but remains opaque at the building level, which is where power constraints and deployment decisions are actually made.

The disclosure gap is structural. Google's policy of publishing only state-level investment figures means individual campuses and their grid dependencies cannot be assessed from published data. For a site whose thesis holds that the grid is now the binding constraint on AI scaling, a major operator withholding facility-level power specifications leaves a critical piece of the constraint analysis unmeasurable.
